newsitem.title: UK: Big crop of UK bank results dominated by NatWest.
newsitem.headline: Big crop of UK bank results dominated by NatWest.

text.p: Next week's big crop of British bank results will be dominated by an expected announcement on investment banking strategy at National Westminster Bank.
The fuss over NatWest will not entirely overshadow the other results with analysts expecting the established British banks to translate higher profits into healthy dividend growth.
Of the major UK banks with large investment banking interests, NatWest is expected to dominate the headlines.

The bank has already said profits will not be more than 770 million pounds in the first half due to the under-performance of its investment banking unit NatWest Markets which reported a net 77 million pounds loss on interest rate options.
Analysts will be looking for a clear statement from NatWest chief executive Derek Wanless who has temporarily taken command at NatWest Markets as to its future strategy.

Many would like to hear the name of Markets' new boss but this is thought unlikely. There has also been speculation that NatWest will remove the Treasury section from Markets and return to the UK bank.
This would make the investment bank unit easier to sell in the longer run if NatWest decides to go down that route.
In the figures, analysts will be looking hard at costs which are expected to be high given spending at NatWest Markets and the costs of restructuring the UK bank.
The other UK bank with major exposure to investment banking is Barclays which at the last full-year stage took a concerted beating over poor results at its investment bank unit BZW.
BZW is expected to have done rather better in the first half than it did in a lacklustre second half of 1996.
In February, Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor warned that costs at BZW would continue at high levels in the first half with improvement in profit beginning to come through in the second
Elsewhere, margins are likely to be tight but the UK bank will benefit from the boom in consumer banking, analysts say.
Barclays headline profits are expected to decline slightly due to lower exceptional gains to around 1.23 to 1.24 billion pounds compared to 1.296 last year.
The final pair of banks are HSBC Holdings and Standard Chartered which have the majority of their business outside the UK.
Counted as the biggest banking group in the world by most measures, HSBC's profits are expected to rise modestly to around or just below the 2.4 billion pounds mark in the first half.
HSBC and StanChart are the only two in the group to be affected by the strength of sterling and in HSBC's case the bank will also show lower exceptional gains.
At the operating level, however, growth is expected to be 10 percent or higher with its Hong Kong business doing well and its UK unit Midland Bank also contributing strongly.

Most of the Far East currency turmoil, mostly in Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines, has occurred since the end of the half-year but HSBC executives are sure to be asked about the effects of this for the rest of the year.
Standard Chartered's headline pre-tax profits are expected to have been more affected by a strong pound since it has very little UK revenue.
Forecasts range around the 440 to 450 million pounds mark after 448 million pounds last time.

Analysts see strong growth in StanChart's core Hong Kong and Malaysia markets but this will be offset by growing costs which the bank has already flagged. -- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8864.
